metadata.title: Manufacture the Wow Moment
metadata.purpose: Walk viewers through a 5-day team adoption playbook for Claude, with the key insight that adoption is a sales problem solved by manufacturing one convincing 'wow' moment before any broad rollout.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: Manufacture the Wow Moment?

beats.narration_text: Shalom. This is Liam, in for Bear. Your team still isn't using Claude. You tried everything. What actually works? Manufacturing one wow moment before you touch anyone else.

props.ask: Why won't my team adopt Claude even after I showed them?
props.answer_preview: Adoption is a sales problem. You need to manufacture the wow moment first.

beats.narration_text: This is a five-day playbook. Monday through Friday. Each day is under an hour. By Friday your team runs on Claude.

card.sub: Monday: Projects. Tuesday: Templates. Wednesday: Wow. Thursday: Convert one. Friday: Roll out.

beats.narration_text: Monday: set up Claude Projects. One project per recurring deliverable — client updates, proposals, meeting recaps, campaign briefs. Each project gets only the context it needs. A gold-standard example, the relevant background doc, and custom instructions generated by Claude itself. Your team probably produces the same five things every week. Build five projects. That's Monday.

illustration.concept: Team Projects setup flow — 5 recurring deliverables each mapped to a separate Claude Project with context loading
illustration.layout: Left: 5 deliverable labels stacked vertically. Right: each connects via arrow to a Project box listing its allowed context. Global instruction node at bottom.

beats.narration_text: Tuesday: create Prompt Templates. One per project. Your teammates open the project, paste their notes into the template, hit enter. No blank chat. No 'what do I type.' Five minutes per project. Tuesday done in under thirty minutes.

card.sub: Prompt Templates mean your teammates always know exactly what to type. The template does the prompting for them.

beats.narration_text: Wednesday: manufacture the wow. Pick one real task you did manually this week. Something that took thirty-plus minutes. Run it through your project. Screenshot the before and after. That screenshot is your proof. Not 'trust me, Claude is good.' Actual side-by-side evidence.

card.sub: Wednesday is the most important day. You build the evidence that sells the rest of the week.

beats.narration_text: Thursday: don't train ten people. Convert one. And pick the right person. Not the tech enthusiast — they'll figure it out alone. Not the biggest skeptic — too much resistance. The person who is drowning. Behind on emails. Always in meetings. Staying late. Sit with them. Run the project on their actual work. Watch their face. That reaction converts the rest of the team.

illustration.concept: Three-person selector diagram: Enthusiast (skip), Skeptic (skip), Drowning colleague (target) with rationale labels
illustration.layout: Three columns, each headed by a role label. Enthusiast and Skeptic have a cross overlay. Drowning has a check and a sub-label: 'uses their real work / 15-min session.'

beats.narration_text: Friday: roll out to the full team. Pre-flight check — projects ready, templates saved, before-after screenshots ready, one teammate who can vouch. Send the message. DM two or three people directly. Your Thursday convert does the same. That's it. One week. No IT ticket. No training session.

card.sub: No IT ticket. No leadership deck. No PowerPoint. Anthropic states Claude does not train on team data.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Block Monday morning right now. Use Claude to identify your team's five recurring deliverables. Create one project before lunch. That first project is the hardest. Everything else follows.

card.sub: Ask Claude: what are my team's five recurring deliverables? Build project one before lunch.

beats.narration_text: Adoption is a sales problem. Manufacture the wow. The rest follows. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to introduce Claude to your team and you need one demonstration that actually changes how they think about it — not a capabilities list, a wow moment. Ask Claude to help you design the demonstration: what task to pick, how to set it up so the output is immediately useful, and how to run it live without it going wrong.

props.command: I want to introduce Claude to my team and I need one demonstration that actually changes how they think about it — not a capabilities list, a concrete wow moment. Help me design the demonstration: what task to pick that will resonate with this team, how to set it up so the output is immediately useful rather than theoretical, and how to run it live without the demo going wrong.
Take what you learned from [Manufacture the Wow Moment] and apply it to your own work. What's one thing you'll try first?
props.runningText: paste this into Claude and run it on your own work…
